values.value: Sheep (predominantly Romney), beef and dairy grazing
About 2,700 stock units: 480 dairy heifers, 70 beef cattle and 1,100 ewes
Take groundwater from one bore to irrigate 118 ha
Free-draining stony silt loams under centre pivot and lateral irrigation. These soils carry most of the farm's pasture and winter forage production.
Deeper, slower-draining silt loams under centre pivot and border-dyke irrigation. They pug easily when wet and are used for most of the winter crop.
Very stony terraces with no irrigation. Pasture growth depends on spring and autumn rain and the land is mostly grazed by cattle.
Flat leased land along the south-east boundary beside the creek. It is poorly drained and is grazed seasonally under a lease.

This plan describes how Tussock Rise Farm manages the risks its farming poses to freshwater, and the actions the owner will take to reduce them. It follows Schedule 7 of the Canterbury Land and Water Regional Plan.

The farm is 248 hectares on the Example Plains, of which 231.5 hectares are grazable. It carries sheep, beef cattle and dairy grazing and grows winter fodder crops on part of the cultivated area.

The highest risks are nitrate leaching on the light soils and terraces, and sediment, phosphorus and microbial loss from the creek flats during winter grazing.

Much of the stock exclusion fencing is done and nutrients are managed from an annual nutrient budget. The remaining actions are in the action table.
Leave critical source areas ungrazed and use a back-fence
Update the chemical inventory and spill kit each season

Install a culvert crossing at the main race

Mark 10 m fertiliser setbacks along the creek
Complete and review the nutrient budget every autumn
Nutrients are matched to crop need from an annual budget, and losses are kept below the GMP Loss Rate.
Nitrogen loss is 21 kg N/ha/yr in the 2025/26 nutrient budget, below the Baseline GMP Loss Rate of 26 and the GMP Loss Rate of 22.
Winter crops are grazed from the top of the paddock down, and catch crops are sown after the winter crop on the light soils.
Critical source areas are left ungrazed in winter and a 10 m grass buffer is kept along the creek and drain.
Winter grazing plan; photos each July
Fertiliser rates come from soil tests every two years and the nutrient budget; no nitrogen is applied from 1 May to 31 July.
Soil tests; fertiliser recommendations and application records
Fertiliser is delivered to the bunded loading pad 80 m from the creek; spreading is by a Spreadmark-certified contractor.
Irrigation is scheduled to soil moisture and the system is checked every year.
No new irrigation system is planned on this farm.
The pivots and the lateral are checked before the season and a uniformity test is done every year.
Annual system check; uniformity test reports
Irrigation is scheduled from soil moisture probes and the weekly water balance; application depth is set for each soil.
The owner and the part-time worker are trained by the irrigation supplier each spring.
Cultivation and winter grazing are planned to keep soil on the farm.
Winter grazing is planned around critical source areas and the creek flats are only grazed in dry conditions.
Cultivation is timed for dry soils, paddocks are re-sown before 31 March and stock come off wet paddocks at an agreed trigger.
The creek and spring-fed drain are fenced, planted and kept clear of stock.
The creek is fenced on one side; the remaining 400 m will be fenced by 1 March 2027.
A 10 m grass margin is kept and 0.8 ha of the creek margin will be planted in natives.
A culvert crossing will replace the ford at the main race; troughs are kept 20 m from the creek.
Tuna and kōura habitat in the creek is protected by fencing, shade planting and no fertiliser in the setbacks.
One offal pit, to be moved; farm rubbish leaves the farm.
Farm rubbish is taken off site; the old offal pit will be moved more than 50 m from the bore and waterways before it is used again.
Pit location on the farm map
Stock water is metered and leaks are fixed quickly.
Stock water is float-controlled and leaks are fixed within a week; the main meter is verified every five years.
Creek margin fencing incomplete; offal pit within 50 m of the bore.
Waterbodies (wetlands, riparian areas, drains, rivers, lakes)
Point sources (offal pits, farm rubbish pits, silage pits)
Keep the creek and spring-fed drain fenced and shaded, and keep fertiliser and chemicals out of the setbacks.

- Tuna (longfin eel) (Creek and lowland river)
- Inanga (Lower river reaches)
- Kōura (Spring-fed headwaters)
- Watercress (Spring-fed drain)
Tussock Rise drains to the creek on its south-east boundary, which joins the Example River below the farm. [to complete: the council's description of the catchment and its main freshwater issues]
